name: Hearthmakers
author: hearthmakers@example.com
description: A Hearthmakers game server: the packaged server (one Linux executable with Node inside) from the Server releases of Hearthmakers/Hearthmakers-Releases. Players add it in the game's Multiplayer window as ws://<address>:<port>; the game in a browser (an https page) needs wss:// through a reverse proxy with a certificate. The server's own panel listens on 127.0.0.1 inside the container only: settings are this egg's variables, commands go in the console (help lists them), and admins also type them in the game's chat. To update, type update in the console, then start the server again.

installation.script:
#!/bin/bash
# Hearthmakers: takes the newest packaged server into the server's folder. Server releases are tagged
# server-<commit> and never marked latest (the latest is the desktop app's), so the newest is picked from the list.
# Only the executable is written: data/, plugins/ and the rest stay as they are on a reinstall.
# It runs on Debian's own stable image, so its packages are always a supported release's.
set -e
apt-get update -qq
apt-get install -y -qq --no-install-recommends curl jq ca-certificates
mkdir -p /mnt/server
cd /mnt/server
URL=$(curl -fsSL "https://api.github.com/repos/Hearthmakers/Hearthmakers-Releases/releases?per_page=30" | jq -r '[.[] | select(.tag_name | startswith("server-"))] | sort_by(.published_at) | last | .assets[]? | select(.name == "hearthmakers-server-linux-x64") | .browser_download_url')
if [ -z "$URL" ]; then
  echo "No Hearthmakers server release was found."
  exit 1
fi
curl -fL -o hearthmakers-server-linux-x64 "$URL"
chmod +x hearthmakers-server-linux-x64
echo "Installed $URL"

variables.name: Server name
variables.description: How the server shows in players' server lists.

variables.name: Message of the day
variables.description: The line under the server's name in players' server lists.
variables.default_value: Welcome! Light the fire, raise a home.

variables.name: Server icon
variables.description: The server's icon in players' server lists.

variables.name: Most players
variables.description: How many players may be on at once.

variables.name: World threads
variables.description: How many threads the worlds are shared among; each holds about 120 MB of its own, so set it by the server's memory. Empty: the machine's cores less one, at most 4 (inside a container that counts the host's cores, not this server's limit).

variables.name: Realm size
variables.description: Side, in blocks, of the realms players make from now on (rounded to an even number, 32 at least); a realm keeps the size it was made with.

variables.name: Characters per account
variables.description: How many characters an account may have, unless an admin grants it more.

variables.name: Realms per account
variables.description: How many realms an account may have, unless an admin grants it more.

variables.name: Experience rate
variables.description: Multiplies the experience pioneers and colonists gain (2 is twice as fast; decimals allowed). The levels' curve stays the game's.

variables.name: Small blueprints per account
variables.description: How many small blueprints an account may keep, unless an admin grants it more.

variables.name: Medium blueprints per account
variables.description: How many medium blueprints an account may keep, unless an admin grants it more.

variables.name: Large blueprints per account
variables.description: How many large blueprints an account may keep, unless an admin grants it more.

variables.name: Chat channels
variables.description: Comma-separated id:scope:Name, the scope global, world or party; global, realm and party need no more than their id.

variables.name: Database address
variables.description: A Postgres to keep the save in (postgres://user:password@host:5432/name). Empty: the save is kept in data/db in the server's folder.
